messages:
ash: Quick brainstorm: what if we move from opaque pilot traffic mirrors to a "slot lease" model for canaries, focusing on clear ownership and predictable drains?

leo: interested. sketch the main primitives pls. how does it play w/ existing affinity rules and rollout knobs?

ash: primitives: Slot = {id, owner, scope, weight_or_qps, ttl}. Arbiter issues leases, routers consult local lease cache. States: active -> draining -> revoked. Draining means no new allocations, in-flight finish.

rachel: concern: long-lived sessions & KV caches. TTLs will be short for safety, but users can have minutes-long sessions.

ash: plan: separate visitor_affinity TTL from slot TTL. i.e., session stickiness survives beyond slot expiry for N minutes to reduce tail effects. also allow canary to request an extension token after warmup metrics pass.

leo: routing ergonomics? stateless routers preferred. do we do consistent hashing w/ per-slot token buckets?

ash: yes, router algo: compute hash for request -> candidate slot / primary decision; if slot has capacity token -> route canary else fallback. routers keep lease cache ttl=5s and listen to arbiter invalidations.

rachel: safety scoring for extensions: need composite signal (latency, error rate, eval regressions). noise robustness is key.

ash: propose scoring window 1m/5m, weighted metrics -> composite score. define bands: safe (0-0.4), degraded (0.4-0.7) -> step down weight, unsafe (>0.7) -> revoke. add cooldown 2m to avoid flip-flop.

nina: op controls: panic button to immediate kill, must be audible in audit log and annotate reason. opsbot should post revoke event.

opsbot: auto: lease slot-202803 revoked by arbiter (composite_score=0.81) reason=high_5xx, action=drain->revoke, trace=arbiter/slot/3632109999

leo: what about partial degradation instead of full revoke? reduce weight from 5% to 1% automatically when score in degraded band. gives time for transient recovery.

ash: agreed. allow policy mapping score bands -> weight delta. route fallback list prioritized: same variant in alternate pool -> primary -> fallback-model.

rachel: semantics for in-flight reqs during revoke? we must avoid cutting them mid-flight and also avoid double-counting metrics when routing shifts.

ash: revoke flow: 1) arbiter marks slot draining and emits event. 2) routers stop assigning new requests to slot. 3) existing requests finish. 4) after drain_timeout slot transitions revoked. metrics pipelines tag metrics with slot-id; post-revoke we stop attributing new metrics to slot.

nina: KV snapshotting before revoke for fast restore? optional, expensive. prefer not default.

leo: testing: simulation of hysteresis + a staging chaos job that toggles slots to validate cooldown.

opsbot: note: add canary extension policy: max_extensions_per_hour, approval_threshold.

ash: next steps: i'll draft a short appendix with proto sketches (lease schema, arbiter RPCs, router cache semantics), include sample YAML config and scoring parameters. nina/leo will draft runbook for panic/drain paths and e2e tests.

rachel: also include a small litmus test in CI that flips revoke and asserts no double attribution and graceful drain.

nina: fine. move to backlog as medium refactor, assign owners.

ash: thanks all, will open PR and ping for reviews.
